page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering balanced compute and memory capacity. It is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing hyperthreading at two threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. The system integrates 120 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by 45 MB of L3 cache. There are no attached local storage disks or GPUs bundled with this instance type, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark data demonstrates typical performance characteristics of older-generation Intel Xeon silicon. Single-threaded benchmarks are consistently limited, with the Geekbench single-core score of 922.0 and stress-ng single-core result placing in the bottom 10% to 25% percentiles. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also trail modern hardware. However, overall multi-core aggregate throughput remains solid across mid-tier percentiles, recording a PassMark CPU score of 20,859.21, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,982.0, and 23,520.43 on multi-core stress-ng tests.

Memory bandwidth measurements highlight 101.81 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 46.41 GB/sec uncached write throughput for large blocks, supporting stable in-memory application performance such as Redis SET operations at 21.91 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 18.23 GB/sec, and database operations score in the average tier. On CPU-based LLM inference, the machine handles smaller models efficiently, delivering 981.05 tokens per second on 135M prompt processing, but throughput drops to poor tiers on large 70B models due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the n1-standard-32 offers predictable dedicated multi-threaded compute across wide core counts, though its per-thread performance is inefficient relative to newer architectures. It is well matched for horizontally parallel workloads, continuous integration builds, backend web serving fleets, caching layers, and intermediate database operations that depend on substantial memory and moderate multi-core capacity rather than extreme per-core speed.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon CPU operating at 2.3 GHz. It delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores, 2 threads per core) alongside 120.0 GB of RAM, equivalent to 3.75 GB per vCPU, with 45 MB of L3 cache. The server includes no bundled local storage disks or GPU hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place single-core execution in lower percentiles, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 922.0 and slow single-threaded compression. In contrast, multi-core and memory evaluations remain firmly in the average tier, demonstrated by a PassMark CPU score of 20,859.21, 21.91 million Redis SET operations per second, and 18.23 GB/sec in static web serving. n1-standard-32 fits distributed application servers, parallel software builds, caching services, and enterprise web workloads that benefit from multi-core parallelization over single-thread performance.
